newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weak, off lows on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weak, off lows on selective buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower on Monday, but off their lows as foreign funds selectively bought blue-chip stocks, dealers and fund managers said.
The benchmark Composite Index shed 2.55 points to end at 1,134.23, after reaching an intraday low of 1,128.35.
"The value is there. It just takes someone to take the first step (to start buying). It's just the sentiment that's negative," said Lynn Cheah Lee Ling, assistant manager at BHLB Asset Management.
Blue-chip stocks Renong, Tan Chong and Sime Darby were among the most active stocks.
Genting ended in positive territory, after "heavy buying" by foreign institutions, said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
Motor distributor Tan Chong closed strongly firmer after announcing a revised version of its restructuring plan that will see the demerger of its group operations.
"Tan Chong is a fundamental 'buy'," said the dealer.

Renong, even though it ended 10 cents lower at 3.72 ringgit, had seen institutional support, dealers said. The company's launch of a housing project in the southern city of Johor Baru has had a strong response, said Cheah.
